paragraphs: Mia and Ben are getting ready for the school book fair on Saturday morning. Mr. Lee usually opens the doors at eight, but it is already 8:10 and the entrance is still closed. Mia asks, “{{mask_1}}?” The fair is in the library, and its sign says it opens on Saturdays. “{{mask_2}}?” Ben asks. They look at the room plan. “{{mask_3}}?” Mia asks as they start moving the tables. One box is very heavy. “{{mask_4}}?” Ben asks. They find the welcome sign in the hallway. “{{mask_5}}?” Mia asks.

Ben opens the supply box, but there is no tape inside. “{{mask_6}}?” Mia asks. They check a small table, which rocks from side to side. “{{mask_7}}?” Ben asks. Mia unrolls a poster. “{{mask_8}}?” she asks, looking at the empty wall above the entrance. Ben looks around but cannot find the markers. “{{mask_9}}?” Mia asks. The snack delivery is due at ten. Ben checks the clock. “{{mask_10}}?”

The children’s book corner is ready, but Ben is not sure which books belong there. “{{mask_11}}?” Mia asks. They have green stickers for the used books. “{{mask_12}}?” Ben asks. Mia reads the price sign, which says five dollars. “{{mask_13}}?” she asks. Ms. Park is their teacher and promised to help at the fair. “{{mask_14}}?” Ben asks when he sees her coat by the desk. They count the chairs beside the tables. “{{mask_15}}?” Mia asks. There are enough for the reading group.

Rain begins outside, so Mia points to the tables near the open door. “{{mask_16}}?” she asks. A van turns into the school driveway, and the driver waves. “{{mask_17}}?” Ben asks. The list says each box holds ten books. “{{mask_18}}?” Mia asks when they reach the last box. The first visitors are expected at nine, and the clock is almost nine. “{{mask_19}}?” Ben asks. Mia sees that the cash box is locked. “{{mask_20}}?” she asks. Ben finds its key on the desk. The doors open, and the first families walk in.
